name: Braun Silk-expert IPL

lead: A home IPL hair-removal device from Braun, described as having a skin-tone sensor.
Sources found cover IPL in general rather than this product.

paras: Pulsed light is absorbed by hair melanin, heating the follicle; multiple sessions are needed.
Burns, redness and pigmentation changes are reported with IPL; manufacturers restrict use to lighter skin tones.

lead: Braun Silk-expert is Braun's home intense pulsed light (IPL) hair-removal line, with versions described as having a skin-tone sensor. Braun is a Procter & Gamble subsidiary, and Wikipedia lists IPL appliances and epilators among its beauty-care products.[1]

IPL heats hair follicles through melanin absorption and requires repeated sessions.[2] Wikipedia cites manufacturer statements that such devices suit light to medium skin tones and work best on darker hair.[2]
No device-specific clinical studies or detailed product sources were found, so this entry is brief.

paras: Braun was founded by Max Braun in Frankfurt in 1921, was acquired by Gillette in stages from 1967, and became a Procter & Gamble subsidiary when P&G acquired Gillette in 2005.[1]

Clinic IPL studies have reported hair reduction of roughly half to two-thirds at six to twelve months; side effects include redness, burns and pigment changes.[2][3] These data do not come from Braun devices.
